title: Check a claim against the bracket

blocks.text: A freight company's depot-siting MILP has been running for an hour. While it runs, managers keep asking the same kind of question: "is there a plan worth at least 5,200?", or, on the cost model, "can we do it for 3,000 or less?". The solver's two numbers answer each question in one of three ways, without waiting for the end.

Write `judge_claim(value, incumbent, bound, maximize)` in `claims.py`. `incumbent` is the value of the best plan found so far, or `None` when no plan has been found yet. `bound` is the best bound. `maximize` is `True` for a maximization and `False` for a minimization. The claim is "a plan at least as good as `value` exists" (at least `value` when maximizing, at most `value` when minimizing). Return:

items: `"found"` when the incumbent already is such a plan: for a maximization `value <= incumbent`, for a minimization `value >= incumbent`.
`"impossible"` when the bound rules it out: for a maximization `value > bound`, for a minimization `value < bound`.
`"possible"` otherwise: the claim lies inside the bracket, and only more search can settle it.

blocks.text: With `incumbent` set to `None`, no claim is `"found"`, and a claim the bound does not rule out is `"possible"`: not having found a plan yet is not a proof that none exists.

cases.says: on a maximization a claim at or below the incumbent is found, one up to the bound is possible, one above the bound is impossible
on a minimization the incumbent is the high end and the bound the low end, so the directions flip
a claim exactly at the bound is possible, since the optimum may sit on the bound
a claim exactly at the incumbent is found, since the incumbent itself reaches it
with no plan found yet, nothing is found and nothing within the bound is ruled out

origin.section: The Incumbent Rises and the Bound Falls Until They Meet

concepts: a MILP run keeps an incumbent, the best plan found, and a best bound no plan can beat, and the optimum lies between them
